cards.explanation: The answer is “Look at the Lamb of God.” John the Baptist sees Jesus walking by and says, “Look, the Lamb of God!” Two of his disciples are with him, and they hear him say it. The day before, John said something close to that, calling Jesus “the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29). If it were me, I'd have just yelled “Hey, it's Him!” and tripped over my own base.
The answer is False. John says, “Look, the Lamb of God!” and the two disciples who hear it follow Jesus. They don't stay put, and there's no meeting about it. They hear it and they go.

The answer is “Where are You staying.” Jesus asks, “What do you want?” and they answer with a question of their own. They call Him “Rabbi” (which means Teacher) and ask, “…where are You staying?” Jesus asks them what they want and they ask for His address. Honestly, friends, that's an answer I respect.

The answer is True. The two followers went, saw where He was staying, and spent that day with Him. The text adds that it was about the tenth hour. Whatever time they showed up, they didn't just peek in and leave.

The answer is True. Andrew first finds his brother Simon and tells him, “We have found the Messiah…” Andrew is the one who heard John's testimony and followed Jesus. He had news, and the first stop was family. I bet he walked fast.

The answer is that Andrew brings Simon to Jesus. He doesn't just tell Simon the news, he brings him to Jesus. Then Jesus looks at Simon, and that's where the story goes next. Most of us would fire off a text with news like that, friends. Andrew brought his brother to Jesus instead.

The answer is Cephas. Jesus says, “You will be called Cephas…” which is translated as Peter. Notice that Jesus says it right after looking at Simon and calling him by his name and his father's name. A whole new name, and it comes as soon as Jesus looks at him.

The answer is “follow.” Jesus finds Philip and says, “Follow Me.” Just two words, and Philip is the one He says them to. Short and sweet. Honestly, friends, my instructions for a cookie batch take longer than that.

The answer is True. Philip tells Nathanael, “We have found the One Moses wrote about in the Law…” Moses is the one God sent to bring His people out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10). Philip adds that this is the One the prophets foretold, too. Philip had a lot to say about Jesus.

The answer is “Can anything good come from Nazareth.” Nathanael asks, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip doesn't argue with him, he just says, “Come and see…” Philip had a good answer, and it was an invitation.
The answer is True. Jesus sees Nathanael coming and says, “Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.” Jesus says it when He sees Nathanael approaching, and what He says is kind.

The answer is under the fig tree. Jesus says, “Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.” Nathanael asked how Jesus knew him, and that was the answer. Think about it, friends. If somebody told me they saw me before I was even called, I'd check my apron for a hidden camera.

The answer is that Nathanael calls Jesus the Son of God. He calls Jesus “Rabbi” and says, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” Earlier he was asking about Nazareth. That's quite a turn. And it all comes right after Jesus tells him what He saw.
The answer is False. Jesus doesn't call the fig tree the biggest thing. He says, “You will see greater things than these.” Even something that amazing is just the start.

The answer is the angels of God. Jesus says, “…you will all see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). Notice He says “…you will all see…” so He's speaking to more than just Nathanael.
